trainers.instruction: Listen to the conversation in the library.

atoms.sound: Hello! Can I ask for your help? I’m looking for a new book to read, but I’m not sure what to choose.
Of course! Let’s walk around and see what might fit your taste. What kind of stories do you usually enjoy?
I normally reed mystery novels, but I want something different. Maybe something funny or exciting. Something that is fun to read.
Do you prefer stories set in the real world, or something with a more unusual setting?
I think I’d like something in the real world. And I like characters who feel believable.
Great, that gives me a clearer picture of your taste.

atoms.a: What kind of story is Dhruv looking for?
atoms.sound: What kind of story is Dhroov looking for?
b: a historical book with many facts

atoms.a: What does “believable characters” mean in this conversation?
b: characters that are easy to understand

atoms.sound: Let’s check the Fiction shelf over here. We just got a few new titles. Here’s one you might like: The Weekend List. It’s about two friends who try to complete a list of challenges before summer ends. It’s fast-paced and funny.
That does sound fun. Do you have anything slightly more serious too? I like stories with a bit of emotion sometimes.
Sure. This one, Running Home, is about a girl who has to move to a new town and slowly finds her place. It’s still easy to read, but the feelings are deeper.

instruction.text: Which picture best matches the book Running Home?

atoms.a: Why might Dhruv decide not to choose The Weekend List?
atoms.sound: Why might Dhroov decide not to choose The Weekend List?
b: ++He wants a story with more emotional depth.
He said he dislikes stories set in the real world.
He prefers books with lots of clues to solve.
He thinks the book is too long.

atoms.sound: We can also take a look over here. We just set up a table with our newest books. Some of them might fit what you’re looking for.
Oh, nice. I like seeing them all together like this. The covers look really different from each other.

Yes, this table has a mix! “A little more you” is a light coming-of-age story. “Shadow Tree” is a horror with a darker tone. And “The Life of Frida Kahlo” is a new biography about the artist’s life and work. Many readers find her story inspiring.
Hmm… interesting. I don’t think I want anything scary, and I don’t want to read a biography either.

instruction.text: Choose which book Dhruv will most likely pick.
instruction.sound: Choose which book Droov will most likely pick.

atoms.sound: A little more you is a great choice. Feel free to read the back cover.
